svg.title: Prefill is fat and short. Decode is thin and long.
svg.desc: A hand-drawn whiteboard whose top band is a single timeline: prefill is one dense block occupying about a ninetieth of it at 0.27 seconds for 1,024 prompt tokens, and decode is a long row of sixty small separate boxes stretching across the rest at 25 seconds for 1,024 generated tokens. Below, the per-token KV-cache formula is written out longhand reaching 512 KiB per token, with a staircase of slabs growing under the decode row and running totals of 2 GiB at 4k and 4 GiB at 8k, beside a crossed-out no-cache loop at 3.2 tokens per second. At the bottom a roofline plot marks the ridge at 208 FLOPs per byte with decode sitting far down the ramp at 2 and prefill on the ceiling at 2,048.
svg.text: Prefill is fat and short. Decode is thin and long.
13.8 TFLOPs of real arithmetic. Cores busy. COMPUTE-BOUND
one token at a time. Cores mostly IDLE, waiting on memory. BANDWIDTH-BOUND
2 (K and V) x 32 layers x 32 kv heads x 128 head dim x 2 bytes
KV CACHE - one more slab per generated token
the GPU is not thinking, it is
...so how do we get decode onto the ramp?
